mainTopic: When a husband becomes impure from his wife's blood or כתם, and when a wife is presumed pure for her husband
overview: The amud opens with the חכמים of יבנה explaining how long 'after a time' is in the משנה. If a woman finds blood before she could get off the bed and rinse her face, she and her husband are טמאין מספק and bring an אשם תלוי. If she waited longer, the husband is impure only through מגע. רבי עקיבא says he is impure as a בועל, and רבי יהודה בנו של רבן יוחנן בן זכאי says he is fully pure. The גמרא uses this ברייתא to raise a קשיא against רב אשי, which stays unanswered. It then defends רבי יהודה's view: he holds like שמאי that there is no backdating, and the case is one where the husband did not finish the act. Next, רב and ריש לקיש argue with שמואל and רבי יוחנן about whether a כתם makes the husband impure going backward or only from now on. The גמרא explains that a כתם differs from מעת לעת because the evidence is right in front of you. A new משנה teaches that wives are presumed pure for their husbands, even husbands back from a trip. The amud ends with a dispute over whether a wife is permitted once her expected period time (וסת) has arrived. That dispute depends on whether וסתות are דאורייתא or דרבנן, and רב אשי's version of it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Checking whose view the questioners follow
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי צדוק asks whether the questioners follow רבי עקיבא, who says the woman makes her husband impure. They answer that they do not hold this view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps you are asking according to רבי עקיבא, who says she makes the man who was with her impure? They said to him: We have not heard (that view).
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering, רבי אליעזר asks what view the questioners hold. They tell him they do not follow רבי עקיבא, so they really need an explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, the husband would be impure as a בועל in any case, so the exact length of 'after a time' would matter less. When they say 'we have not heard,' they are rejecting that approach. This sets up the real answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
She makes (someone) impure
The man who had relations with her
We have not heard. Here it means: we do not accept this as the הלכה

phrases.english: Perhaps you are saying according to Rabbi Akiva
that she makes impure the man who had relations with her?
phrases.notes: Just as she makes impure the pure things she touched during the past day, he is asking whether her husband is impure too.

phrases.english: They said to him: We have not heard (this).
phrases.notes: They mean they don't follow this view, so they still need to know what 'after a time' means.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from before this section: the חכמים of אושא asked רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי צדוק what 'לאחר זמן' means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are the questioners asking according to רבי עקיבא's view, which makes the husband impure as a בועל?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. They do not hold like רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Yavne's explanation: the short time is still 'within the time'
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the חכמים of יבנה: if she did not wait as long as it takes to get off the bed and rinse her face, it counts as within the time. Both are impure out of doubt, exempt from a קרבן, and obligated in an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: This is how the Sages in Yavne explained it. If she did not wait as long as it takes to get down from the bed and rinse her face, this is within the time. They are impure out of doubt, exempt from an offering, and obligated in a provisional guilt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר gives the real answer by quoting the חכמים of יבנה. He defines the short time period the משנה was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The measure is how long it takes to get out of bed and rinse her face. Within that short time, the blood may have come during relations, but we are not sure. So they are טמאין מספק and bring an אשם תלוי, not a חטאת, because a חטאת is brought only for a sin that definitely happened.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who sat in יבנה, an earlier generation than those in אושא
She waited (before examining herself)
Within the time period, which is close enough to relations to raise a doubt
Impure because of a doubt
Exempt from an offering (a חטאת)
A 'hanging' guilt offering, brought when someone is unsure whether they sinned

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the wording. The משנה calls this short delay 'לאחר זמן' (after a time), but here it is called 'תוך זמן' (within the time). They are the same case: a short delay that still leaves a doubt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical measure for the משנה's vague phrase 'after a time.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: כָּךְ פֵּרְשׁוּ חֲכָמִים בְּיַבְנֶה:
phrases.english: He said to them: This is how the Sages in Yavne explained it:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁהֲתָה כְּדֵי שֶׁתֵּרֵד מִן הַמִּטָּה
phrases.english: If she did not wait as long as it takes to get down from the bed
and rinse her face —
this is within the time,
phrases.notes: This is the time the משנה called 'after a time.'

phrases.english: and they are impure out of doubt,
and they are exempt from an offering,
and they are obligated in a provisional guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that he knows they don't follow רבי עקיבא, he answers their original question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the time period called 'לאחר זמן' in the משנה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is less than the time it takes to get off the bed and rinse her face. In that time both are טמאין מספק and bring an אשם תלוי.

steps.title: Waiting longer than that counts as 'after the time'
steps.stepSummary: If she waited as long as it takes to get off the bed and rinse her face, it is 'after the time.' The משנה's doubt case no longer applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she waited as long as it takes to get down from the bed and rinse her face, this is after the time.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the other half of יבנה's explanation: what happens if she waited longer than the short time. It sets up the ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she has waited this long, the blood is no longer close enough to relations to create the doubt that requires an אשם תלוי. The next step explains what impurity the husband still has.

keyTerms.meaning: That she gets down from the bed
She rinses her face
After the time, meaning past the short window of doubt

phrases.english: If she waited as long as it takes to get down from the bed
and rinse her face —
this is after the time.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁהֲתָה כְּדֵי שֶׁתֵּרֵד מִן הַמִּטָּה וְתָדִיחַ אֶת פָּנֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the opposite case to step 2: a longer wait instead of a short one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Waiting as long as it takes to get off the bed and rinse her face puts the case 'after the time,' outside the משנה's doubt case.

steps.title: The husband is impure through contact only, and רבי עקיבא disagrees
steps.stepSummary: In the 'after the time' case, and also after a full day or between two examinations, the husband becomes impure only through מגע and not as a בועל. רבי עקיבא says he is impure as a בועל too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same is true when she waited a full 24 hours, or from one examination to the next: the man who was with her becomes impure because of contact, but not because of relations. רבי עקיבא says: He even becomes impure because of relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the husband's status in these later cases. Then it brings רבי עקיבא's opinion, which disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מגע impurity lasts only until evening, while בועל impurity lasts seven days. The first opinion treats the husband like any pure item she touched during the earlier period. רבי עקיבא is stricter and gives the husband the full seven days. This is the view the questioners said in step 1 that they do not follow.

keyTerms.meaning: A full 24-hour period
From one examination to the next
Because of contact (impure until evening)
Because of having relations (impure for seven days)

phrases.english: And likewise when she waited a full 24 hours
or from one examination to the next,
the man who was with her becomes impure because of contact,
but he does not become impure because of relations.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אַף מְטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם בּוֹעֵל.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: He even becomes impure because of relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical result of the 'after the time' case from step 3, adds similar cases, and brings רבי עקיבא's opposing view, which was mentioned in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In these later cases the husband is impure only through מגע. רבי עקיבא says he is also impure as a בועל.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two levels of impurity for the husband: מגע, which lasts until evening, and בועל, which lasts seven days. The first opinion gives only מגע here, and רבי עקיבא gives בועל.

steps.title: The most lenient view: the husband may enter the Sanctuary
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בנו של רבן יוחנן בן זכאי says the husband is not impure at all, so he may enter the היכל and offer קטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה, son of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, says: Her husband may enter the Sanctuary and burn incense.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion is brought, and it is the most lenient one. The husband is completely pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the husband is not impure even through מגע, not even until evening. So if he is a כהן, he may enter the היכל and offer the קטורת. This gives three views: impure through מגע only, impure as a בועל, or completely pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Her husband
The Sanctuary in the בית המקדש
Burns the incense offering

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai, says:
Her husband may enter the Sanctuary and burn incense.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third, most lenient opinion to the disagreement in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband is completely pure and may enter the היכל and offer קטורת.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views about the husband: impure through מגע (the first opinion), impure as a בועל (רבי עקיבא), or completely pure (רבי יהודה בנו של רבן יוחנן בן זכאי).

steps.title: The ברייתא fits רב חסדא but seems to contradict רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: With רב חסדא's short time measure, it makes sense that the רבנן call the husband pure. With רב אשי's longer measure, it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works for רב חסדא: that is why the רבנן say he is pure. But for רב אשי, why do the רבנן say he is pure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the ברייתא with the two earlier opinions about how long 'within the time' lasts. It challenges רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב חסדא, 'within the time' is only as long as reaching out and checking. So getting off the bed and cleaning herself is already 'after the time,' and the husband is not a בועל. For רב אשי, a woman with a cloth in her hand is still 'within the time' while she gets off the bed and cleans herself. The husband should then be impure as a בועל, so why does the ברייתא call him pure?

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for (one opinion); this opens a contrast with another opinion
But (for the other opinion)... why? This is where the challenge lands
They rule him pure

steps.confusionAlert: 'מטהרי רבנן' here means the husband is not impure as a בועל, with a seven-day impurity. In step 4, the רבנן still made him impure through מגע.

phrases.english: It works well according to Rav Ḥisda,
phrases.notes: רב חסדא said 'within the time' lasts only as long as it takes her to reach out and check herself.

phrases.english: that is why the Rabbis rule him pure.
But according to Rav Ashi,
phrases.notes: רב אשי said that if she has a cloth in her hand, the time it takes her to get off the bed and clean herself still counts as 'within the time.'

phrases.english: why do the Rabbis rule him pure?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא, הַיְינוּ דִּמְטַהֲרִי רַבָּנַן. אֶלָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי, אַמַּאי מְטַהֲרִי רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from steps 2-4 to test the two definitions of 'within the time.'
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's measure of 'within the time'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats the time to get off the bed and clean herself as 'after the time.' רב אשי treats that same time as 'within the time.'

steps.title: Saying the ברייתא is about a woman without a cloth does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא is about a woman who has no cloth in her hand, then rejects this. If that were so, the ברייתא should have taught both cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the ברייתא is about a case where she has no cloth in her hand: then it should have said 'cloth in her hand' and 'no cloth in her hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible defense of רב אשי and then knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רב אשי agrees that without a cloth, the time is shorter. So one could say the ברייתא is only talking about that case. But then the ברייתא should have split the two cases clearly. It gave one rule with no split, so this defense fails.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say; introduces a possible answer
A checking cloth
It should have said

phrases.english: And if you would say: it is where there is no cloth in her hand,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי ״עֵד בְּיָדָהּ״ וְ״אֵין עֵד בְּיָדָהּ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: then it should have taught 'a cloth in her hand' and 'no cloth in her hand'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises and rejects a possible answer to the challenge in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested defense that the ברייתא is about a case with no cloth in her hand.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא gives no split between having a cloth and not having one, which it would need to do.

steps.title: The challenge to רב אשי stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא is a difficulty for רב אשי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this section. The question on רב אשי has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' means the question still stands. Unlike 'תיובתא,' it is not a full knockout, but no answer is given.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a difficulty; the question remains unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא fits רב חסדא's short measure of 'within the time.' It leaves רב אשי's longer measure with an unanswered קשיא.

phrases.english: It is a difficulty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge once the defense in step 7 has failed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אשי's view is left with an unresolved difficulty from the ברייתא.

steps.title: Why isn't the husband impure for touching her during the מעת לעת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה בנו של רבן יוחנן בן זכאי again and asks why the husband is not impure. He touched her within the 24 hours before she found blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בנו של רבן יוחנן בן זכאי says: her husband may enter the היכל and offer קטורת. But why not say he is impure because he touched a נדה during the מעת לעת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the last opinion in the ברייתא. It repeats that opinion in order to challenge it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים decreed that when a woman finds blood, things she touched in the previous 24 hours become impure looking back. The husband touched her within that window. So how can רבי יהודה say he is completely pure and may serve in the היכל?

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary in the בית המקדש
Incense offered in the היכל
Why not derive it from (a different reason)?
The 24-hour period before she found blood, which becomes impure looking back

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai, says:
her husband may enter the Sanctuary and burn incense.
But let him be impure because he is one who touched
a menstruating woman within the twenty-four-hour period!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּהָוֵה נוֹגֵעַ בְּמֵעֵת לְעֵת שֶׁבְּנִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the opinion from step 5 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה בנו של רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's ruling that the husband is fully pure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule of מעת לעת should make him impure looking back, since he touched her within the 24 hours.

steps.title: He holds like שמאי: impurity starts only when she sees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה בנו של רבן יוחנן בן זכאי holds like שמאי, that every woman becomes impure only from the moment she sees blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said this rule holds like שמאי, who said: for all women, their time is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9. The husband is not impure because this תנא holds like שמאי, who does not go back 24 hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 asked: he touched her within the 24 hours before she found blood, so why isn't he impure? The answer is that, according to שמאי, a woman's impurity starts only when she sees blood. It does not reach back 24 hours. So relations before she saw blood do not make the husband impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Their time is enough: a woman becomes impure only from the moment she sees blood, not before.
A 24-hour period: the opposing view that her impurity reaches back 24 hours.

phrases.english: He who said [this] holds like שמאי,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יהודה בנו של רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, from step 9.

phrases.english: who said: for all women, their time is enough.
phrases.notes: Meaning she counts as impure only from the moment she sees blood, with no worry about earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the view to a specific תנא (שמאי) who rejects backdating impurity.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the 24-hour backdating rule (מעת לעת) applies, so the husband should be impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: This תנא follows שמאי, so there is no backdating and the husband stays pure.

steps.title: But he should be impure as a בעל קרי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: even without her blood, the husband had relations, so he should be impure as a בעל קרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him get it from the fact that he is a בעל קרי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem. Even if her blood does not make him impure, having relations should make him a בעל קרי, who is impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בנו של רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said the husband may go into the היכל and offer קטורת. But someone who had relations with an emission is impure until evening. So how can he be called completely pure?

keyTerms.meaning: A man who had a seminal emission. He is impure until evening.
Let him get it from: why not reach the same result from a simpler reason?

phrases.english: But let him get it [his impurity]
from the fact that he is a בעל קרי!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 10 removed the blood-based impurity, the גמרא points to a different source of impurity.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim of רבי יהודה בנו של רבן יוחנן בן זכאי that the husband is completely pure and may offer קטורת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Relations normally make the man a בעל קרי, who is impure, so he cannot be fully pure.

steps.title: He did not finish the act
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is where the husband did not finish the act, so he is not a בעל קרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The case is] where he did not finish his act of relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 11. It explains the case so the husband never became a בעל קרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The impurity of a בעל קרי comes from an emission. If he stopped before finishing, there was no emission. So nothing makes him impure, and the ruling that he is completely pure stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Finished his act of relations, meaning with an emission.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה בנו של רבן יוחנן בן זכאי holds like שמאי, so there is no backdating. He also speaks of a husband who did not finish the act, so the husband is fully pure.

phrases.english: [The case is] where he did not finish his act of relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed normal, completed relations, which make him a בעל קרי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling is about relations that were not completed, so he never became a בעל קרי.

steps.title: רב: a כתם makes the husband impure going backward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line in the משנה where the חכמים agree with רבי עקיבא about a woman who finds a כתם. רב says the husband becomes impure even for relations from before she found it, following רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים agree with רבי עקיבא about a woman who finds a כתם. רב said: [she makes him impure] going backward, and this follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה and gives רב's explanation of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that even the חכמים agree a woman who finds a כתם passes impurity to the man who had relations with her. רב says this reaches back to relations before she found the stain. That fits רבי מאיר, who holds that a כתם makes things impure going backward.

keyTerms.meaning: A blood stain found on a woman's body or clothing.
Going backward: the impurity also covers the time before it was found.
The חכמים agree: even those who argue elsewhere accept this case.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. A כתם is a stain she finds, not blood she feels or sees coming out. The rules for backdating can be different for each.

phrases.english: And the חכמים agree with רבי עקיבא
about a woman who finds a stain,
phrases.notes: The משנה means she makes the man who had relations with her impure.

phrases.english: רב said: [she makes him impure] going backward,
and this follows רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּרוֹאָה כֶּתֶם, אָמַר רַב לְמַפְרֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, the משנה means a woman who finds a כתם makes her husband impure even for relations from before she found it, following רבי מאיר.

steps.title: שמואל: only from now on
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the משנה means she makes him impure only for relations after she finds the כתם, following the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: from now on, and this follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives שמואל's explanation of the same line in the משנה. He disagrees with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב read the משנה as reaching backward. שמואל reads it as covering only relations after the stain was found. That fits the רבנן, who hold that a כתם makes things impure only from that moment on.

keyTerms.meaning: From now on: impurity only from the moment of finding, with no backdating.

phrases.english: And שמואל said: from now on,
phrases.notes: He means only relations after she found the stain make the man impure.

phrases.english: and this follows the רבנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא, וְרַבָּנַן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing explanation to רב's view in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל, the משנה means a woman who finds a כתם makes her husband impure only for relations after she found it, following the רבנן.

steps.title: But from now on is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: why would the משנה need to teach that relations after finding a כתם make him impure? That seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: From now on? That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's reading. It is setting up the next move, where it will explain what the משנה is adding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she has already found a כתם, she is impure. Of course a man who has relations with her afterward becomes impure. So if the משנה only means that, it seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious: why would the source need to teach this?

phrases.english: From now on? That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading שמואל gave in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's explanation that the משנה refers only to relations after the כתם was found.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה should not need to teach something obvious, and impurity from relations after finding a stain is obvious.

steps.title: Why the משנה had to teach that a כתם makes the husband impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה needed to say this. Otherwise we might have compared a כתם to מעת לעת, which does not make the husband impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since מעת לעת is a rabbinic law, and כתמים are a rabbinic law, then just as מעת לעת does not make her husband impure, כתמים also do not make him impure. So the משנה teaches us that they do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 15 by showing why someone might have thought a כתם does not make the husband impure at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two rules are both דרבנן: the rule that a woman is impure back 24 hours (מעת לעת), and the rule that a כתם makes her impure. מעת לעת does not make the husband impure as a בועל (seven days), even though step 4 says he still gets מגע impurity. So we might have said the same about a כתם. The משנה tells us not to make that comparison, so the lesson is not obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said / thought (it introduces a mistaken idea the text wants to block)
The rule that a woman who sees blood is impure back over the previous 24 hours
A law made by the חכמים, not from the תורה
The man who had relations with her
It teaches us (this is what the משנה comes to teach)

phrases.english: You might have said:
Since the twenty-four-hour period is rabbinic,
and stains are rabbinic —

phrases.aramaic: מָה מֵעֵת לְעֵת לֹא מְטַמְּאָה אֶת בּוֹעֲלָהּ,
phrases.english: just as the twenty-four-hour period does not make impure the man who had relations with her,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כְּתָמִים — לֹא מְטַמְּאָה אֶת בּוֹעֲלָהּ,
phrases.english: so too stains do not make impure the man who had relations with her,
so it teaches us that they do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 15 against שמואל's reading
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: the משנה blocks a mistaken comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כתם is like מעת לעת, since both are דרבנן, so neither makes the husband impure
steps.terutzMaskana: A כתם does make the husband impure for relations after she finds it

steps.title: Maybe the comparison is actually correct
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the comparison is correct, and a כתם really should not make the husband impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it is indeed so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It asks why we should not accept the comparison to מעת לעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 16 said the משנה blocks the comparison. The גמרא now asks what is wrong with that comparison, since both laws are דרבנן. This sets up the next step, which will show a real difference between them.

keyTerms.meaning: But say it is indeed so (a challenge suggesting the rejected idea is actually right)

phrases.english: But say that it is indeed so!
phrases.notes: He means: maybe a כתם really does not make the husband impure, just like מעת לעת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison raised in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a כתם must be treated differently from מעת לעת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both are rabbinic laws, so the comparison seems reasonable

steps.title: With a כתם, the evidence is right in front of you
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the difference: with מעת לעת there was no evidence of impurity at the time, but with a כתם the blood is right there.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, with מעת לעת, there is no 'slaughtered ox in front of you.' Here, with a כתם, there is a 'slaughtered ox in front of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that a כתם and מעת לעת are not really alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With מעת לעת, she had not yet seen any blood when they had relations, so the evidence did not exist yet, and the חכמים did not give the husband the seven-day impurity of a בועל. With a כתם, actual blood is sitting on the cloth, and that clear evidence is why the husband becomes impure as a בועל.

keyTerms.meaning: A slaughtered ox is in front of you: a saying meaning the evidence is right here
There / here (comparing two cases)

steps.whatToRemember: A כתם makes the husband impure even though it is דרבנן, because the blood is clearly there. מעת לעת does not, because no blood existed yet at the time.

phrases.english: There, there is no "slaughtered ox in front of you,"
phrases.notes: This is a saying: the proof is lying right in front of you. With מעת לעת, there was no blood yet.

phrases.english: here there is a "slaughtered ox in front of you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: חילוק: distinguishing the two rabbinic laws
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כתם and מעת לעת are the same because both are דרבנן
steps.terutzMaskana: A כתם is clear, present evidence of impurity, so the husband becomes impure; מעת לעת has no such evidence

steps.title: ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן argue the same way as רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says, like רב, that the husband is impure for relations from before the כתם was found, following רבי מאיר. רבי יוחנן says, like שמואל, that he is impure only from then on, following the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said ריש לקיש: going backward, and it follows רבי מאיר. רבי יוחנן said: from now on, and it follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the same disagreement between רב and שמואל also appears between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words וכן אמר show that ריש לקיש matches רב's view: the husband is impure even for earlier relations. רבי יוחנן matches שמואל's view: only relations after she found the כתם count. So two pairs of אמוראים argue about the same question.

keyTerms.meaning: Going backward in time, for things that happened before
From now on only
And so said (another אמורא holds the same view)

steps.whatToRemember: רב and ריש לקיש say the husband is impure going backward (רבי מאיר). שמואל and רבי יוחנן say only from now on (רבנן).

phrases.english: And so said Reish Lakish:
phrases.notes: "And so" means he says the same as רב from step 13.

phrases.english: Going backward, and it follows Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
From now on, and it follows the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel disagreement matching the views of רב and שמואל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש: the husband is impure going backward (רבי מאיר); רבי יוחנן: only from now on (רבנן)

steps.title: New משנה: all wives are presumed pure for their husbands
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that every wife is presumed pure for her husband, even when he comes back from a trip.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All women are presumed pure for their husbands. Men who come back from a trip: their wives are presumed pure for them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: a husband does not need to check whether his wife is pure before relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman keeps her status of purity unless we know something changed. Even if the husband was away and does not know what happened while he was gone, he may rely on that status.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
A presumed status of purity
Those coming back from a journey

phrases.english: MISHNA: All women
are presumed pure for their husbands,
those men coming back from a journey —
their wives are presumed pure for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי' כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים בְּחֶזְקַת טׇהֳרָה לְבַעְלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All wives are presumed pure for their husbands, even husbands coming back from a journey

steps.title: Why mention husbands returning from a trip?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה had to add the case of husbands coming back from a trip.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why did the משנה need to teach the case of 'those coming back from a trip'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the new משנה by asking why one detail was needed. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said every wife is presumed pure for her husband. So the extra words 'even those coming back from a trip' seem unnecessary, and the גמרא wants to know what they add.

keyTerms.meaning: Why did he need to teach it? A question about extra wording
Those coming back from a trip

phrases.english: גמרא:
Why does he need to teach
'those coming back from a trip'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה quoted in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the phrase 'those coming back from a trip' add to the משנה?

steps.title: Without it, we would think she only checks when he is home
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought the presumption of purity only works when the husband is in town, because then she keeps checking herself. The משנה teaches that it works even when he was away.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: this rule applies only when the husband is in the city, because then she takes it on herself and checks. But when he is not in the city, she does not take it on herself, so the rule would not apply. The משנה teaches us that it still applies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the extra words prevent a mistake. Without them, we would think a wife is only presumed pure when her husband is around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason a wife is presumed pure is that she stays ready for her husband and checks herself. One could argue that when he is away she has no reason to check, so the presumption falls away. The משנה tells us that even so, she keeps her חזקת טהרה.

keyTerms.meaning: It could have entered your mind to say: what we would have wrongly thought
She takes it upon herself (to be ready and check)
In the city (in town)
It teaches us: the משנה's actual point

steps.whatToRemember: A wife keeps her presumption of purity even when her husband comes back from a trip, even though she may not have been checking while he was away.

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:
This applies only where he is in the city,
since she takes it on herself and checks,
but where he is not in the city,
since she does not take it on herself, it would not apply.
So it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra case teaches that the presumption of purity holds even when the husband was away and she had no reason to check.

steps.title: Only if he returns within her expected time
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, quoting רבי יהודה נשיאה, limits the rule: it applies only if the husband returns while she is still within the days before her period is expected.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי יהודה נשיאה: This applies only when he came and found her within the days of her expected time.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש adds a limit to the rule about a husband coming back from a trip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he returns before her next period would normally come, he can assume nothing has changed. But if that time has already passed, we assume her period came as usual. Then he cannot rely on her presumption of purity unless she checked and found herself pure.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is only when: introduces a limit on a rule
The days of her expected time, before her next period is expected

steps.confusionAlert: This is not cancelling the משנה's rule. It only narrows when the presumption of purity can be relied on after a trip.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda Nesia:
And this is only when he came and found her
within the days of her expected time.
phrases.notes: He means she is still in the stretch before her next period would normally arrive.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהוּא שֶׁבָּא וּמְצָאָהּ בְּתוֹךְ יְמֵי עוֹנָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the rule just explained in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A returning husband may rely on his wife's presumption of purity only if he comes back while she is still within her expected time.

steps.title: רב הונא limits the rule to a woman without a fixed cycle
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the presumption of purity was taught only for a woman without a fixed cycle. If she has a fixed cycle, relations are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: They taught this only when she has no fixed cycle. But if she has a fixed cycle, it is forbidden to have relations.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives his own limit on the משנה's rule. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא splits the rule by whether the woman has a וסת (fixed cycle). He says the presumption of purity works only without a fixed cycle, which sounds backwards. The גמרא will question this right away.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught it only in this case: limits a rule
A fixed, regular menstrual cycle
To have marital relations

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין לָהּ וֶסֶת,
phrases.english: They taught this only where she has no fixed cycle,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יֵשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת — אָסוּר לְשַׁמֵּשׁ.
phrases.english: but if she has a fixed cycle, it is forbidden to have relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין לָהּ וֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new limit on the משנה's rule, from a different אמורא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The presumption of purity applies only to a woman without a fixed cycle; with a fixed cycle relations are forbidden.

steps.title: The opposite makes more sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא: a woman without a fixed cycle might have seen blood, while a woman with a fixed cycle knows when her period comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which way is this going? On the contrary, the opposite makes sense! If she has no fixed cycle, say she saw blood. If she has a fixed cycle, her cycle is set for her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's statement, arguing he has it backwards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman without a fixed cycle could get her period at any time, so we should worry she already saw blood. A woman with a fixed cycle knows exactly when it will come, so she should be the one presumed pure until then. So רב הונא's rule seems reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: Which way is this going? It means you have it backwards
On the contrary
The opposite makes sense
Her cycle is fixed for her

phrases.english: Which way is this going?
phrases.notes: This is a way of showing surprise. The statement seems to be turned the wrong way around.

phrases.english: On the contrary, the opposite makes sense!
If she has no fixed cycle, say she saw blood,

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָהּ וֶסֶת — וֶסֶת קְבִיעַ לַהּ!
phrases.english: if she has a fixed cycle, her cycle is set for her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב הונא's statement in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that the presumption of purity applies only to a woman without a fixed cycle.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Logic points the other way: without a fixed cycle she may already have seen blood, while with a fixed cycle she knows when she will become impure and is pure until then.

steps.title: רב הונא's ruling restated: forbidden once her expected period time has come
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the first version of רב הונא and restates it. The presumption of purity applies only before her expected period time. Once that time arrives, she is forbidden, because רב הונא holds וסתות are דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if רב הונא said something, this is what he said: the rule was taught only when the time of her period had not yet arrived. If the time of her period did arrive, she is forbidden. He holds that וסתות are a Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The question in step 25 knocked down the first version of רב הונא. So the גמרא now gives a new version of what he actually said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old version split the cases by fixed cycle versus no fixed cycle, and that made no sense. The new version splits by timing: before her expected period, the presumption of purity works. After her expected period has come, it does not. The reason is that he treats the expected period as a Torah-level concern, so we must worry that she saw blood at that time.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, it was said like this. A formula for replacing a rejected version of a statement with a corrected one.
They taught this only... (limits a rule to a specific case)
The expected time of her period
She is forbidden (to her husband)
He holds / his reasoning is
The expected-period times are a Torah-level matter

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 24. The first version of רב הונא split cases by fixed cycle versus no fixed cycle, and it was rejected. This new version splits cases by whether her expected time had already arrived.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic dispute: is the expected period time (וסת) a Torah concern or a rabbinic one? The practical outcome depends on that question.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this:
Rav Huna says:
They taught this only
when the time of her period had not arrived,
phrases.notes: Some versions say שעת (round brackets) and some say עת (square brackets). Both mean 'the time of'.

phrases.english: but if the time of her period had arrived, she is forbidden.
He holds: periods are by Torah law.
phrases.notes: Since it is a Torah concern, we cannot just assume she stayed pure through her expected time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25 by replacing רב הונא's statement with a new version.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restating the statement (the earlier version is rejected and a new formulation is given)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא divided between a woman with a fixed cycle and one without, which made no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא divides by timing: before her expected period she is permitted, after it has arrived she is forbidden, because וסתות are דאורייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The presumption of purity holds only before her expected period time. Once that time has arrived, she is forbidden.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה: permitted even after her expected period time
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה disagrees with רב הונא. Even if her expected period time has arrived, she is permitted, because he holds וסתות are only דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: even if the time of her period arrived, she is still permitted. He holds that וסתות are a rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: A second sage argues on רב הונא's new version and permits her even after her expected time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument depends on the level of the וסת rule. If it is only rabbinic, the presumption that she stayed pure is strong enough to permit her. The whole difference between רב הונא and רבה בר בר חנה comes down to דאורייתא versus דרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
She is permitted
The expected-period times are only a rabbinic matter

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: once her expected time arrives she is forbidden, because וסתות are דאורייתא. רבה בר בר חנה: she is still permitted, because וסתות are דרבנן.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana says:
Even if the time of her period had arrived,
she is also permitted;
he holds: periods are by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ הִגִּיעַ שְׁעַת וִסְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רב הונא's restated ruling in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after her expected period time has arrived, she is permitted, because וסתות are דרבנן.

steps.title: רב אשי starts a different version of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי introduces his own way of teaching the dispute, beginning with רב הונא's words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי teaches it this way: רב הונא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us that רב אשי has a different version, and his actual words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is ruled here yet. The line opens another version of how רב הונא and רבה בר בר חנה argued, so the learner should expect a change from steps 26 and 27.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it this way (introduces a different version of a teaching)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi teaches it like this:
Rav Huna says:

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי מַתְנֵי הָכִי, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an alternative version of the dispute presented in steps 26 and 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: introduces רב אשי's version of רב הונא's statement, which continues next.
